title: HTTP method and verb differences
content:
1.2 If your application relies on safe HTTP methods (GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS) for state‑changing actions, you should explicitly reflect that in your policy – e.g., by requiring a Fetch‑Metadata header review for requests to those endpoints.

Safe HTTP methods should not be used for state-changing requests.

Check if the given HTTP method requires CSRF protection

Only cross-site-requests that are allowed in Lax mode have top-level navigations and use safe HTTP methods.

Some applications enforce access controls at the platform layer. they do this by restricting access to specific URLs and HTTP methods based on the user's role.

The function csrfSafeMethod() defined below will filter out the safe HTTP methods and only add the header to unsafe HTTP methods.
